title: Validator‑Guided Repair on a Shared Initial LLM Candidate: A Preregistered Paired Evaluation for Network Configuration Safety
abstract: We report a fully preregistered paired confirmatory evaluation (PREREG‑CAND‑001‑VER‑GVR‑2026‑09‑01) that measured the downstream effect of a deterministic validator plus an allowed single automated repair on the same single sampled LLM candidate per intent (shared_initial_candidate semantics). Using the declared generator gpt‑5‑mini and a deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) over a fixed synthetic intent bank (N=200 paired intents; planned_episode_count = 400; completed_episode_count = 400; model_calls_used = 200), every shared candidate passed the validator and therefore no repairs were attempted (repair_attempt_count = 0; repair_applied_count = 0). Observed outcomes were identical across conditions: baseline_success_count = 200/200 and guarded_success_count = 200/200 (n11 = 200, n10 = 0, n01 = 0, n00 = 0); exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0; paired bootstrap (seed = 1729; 10,000 resamples) 95% percentile CI = [0.0, 0.0]. We present artifact‑grounded accounting, representative validator traces, and a focused discussion clarifying the causal meaning of results under shared_initial_candidate semantics and concrete preregistered follow‑on designs required to evaluate repair efficacy under independent sampling or adversarial stress. All principal numbers, tool identifiers, and preregistration metadata are taken directly from archived execution artifacts.

sections.introduction:
Generative language models are increasingly proposed for intent→configuration NetOps workflows where an operator's high‑level intent is translated into device configuration commands. Unverified LLM outputs can contain syntactic errors, logical violations of workflow constraints (e.g., bringing down required redundancy), or hallucinated fields; any of these can cause operational harm if executed. A common mitigation proposal is a generate–validate–repair (GVR) pipeline: an LLM generates candidates, a deterministic verifier checks conformance to intent and workflow constraints, and a repair module attempts to fix flagged violations. Prior demonstrations of verifier‑guided repair in adjacent domains (infrastructure‑as‑code, program repair) motivate studying whether GVR reduces executable misconfiguration rates in NetOps. However, empirical claims about the effect of a validator and repair depend crucially on how sampling is performed: when an experiment reuses the same sampled candidate across baseline and guarded arms (shared_initial_candidate semantics), any paired difference must arise solely from downstream validation/repair on that fixed candidate; generation variability cannot contribute.

This paper reports a preregistered paired confirmatory study that executed exactly that estimand: the effect of deterministic validation and at most one automated repair on the same single sampled candidate per intent. Our contributions are (1) a complete preregistered execution and artifact bundle for the shared_initial_candidate estimand (PREREG‑CAND‑001‑VER‑GVR‑2026‑09‑01); (2) transparent, artifact‑grounded numerical results showing a degenerate null paired effect in this run and diagnostic traces explaining why; and (3) concrete, artifact‑grounded recommendations for follow‑on preregistered designs that can evaluate repair efficacy under independent sampling, higher difficulty, or adversarial conditions.
sections.related_work: Surveys and empirical analyses document hallucination and reference unreliability as pervasive reliability problems for LLMs, motivating grounding and verification in operational pipelines [1]. Evidence‑grounded and retrieval‑augmented pipelines reduce hallucination for QA and documentation tasks in operations domains but typically do not report device‑level executability in packet‑level or CLI emulation environments [2]. Verifier‑guided generation and verifier feedback loops have been shown to improve correctness in infrastructure‑as‑code and program generation settings (e.g., TerraFormer and related systems), demonstrating that deterministic verification feedback can reduce incorrect generated artifacts in those domains; however, the supplied literature lacks a directly comparable device‑execution evaluation in NetOps [3]. NetOps‑specific LLM capability evaluations emphasize intent translation and capability metrics rather than standardized execution‑level safety benchmarks; this methodological gap motivated our preregistered, execution‑grounded study design [4,5]. We position this work narrowly as an artifact‑grounded, confirmatory test of validator/repair effects under explicitly shared sampling semantics rather than a broad claim about GVR general efficacy across models, datasets, or deployment regimes.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. The study was preregistered before any model calls (PREREG‑CAND‑001‑VER‑GVR‑2026‑09‑01). The primary estimand is the paired difference in proportions of validator‑valid executable configurations between guarded (validator + ≤1 repair) and baseline (no validator/repair) under shared_initial_candidate semantics. Analysis followed the preregistered plan: exact two‑sided McNemar on the 2×2 paired contingency table and a paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (bootstrap_seed = 1729; resamples = 10,000). The preregistration specified contamination detection (exact SHA256 matches and high‑similarity n‑gram thresholds), complete_pair_primary missingness handling, sensitivity analyses, and the permitted maximum of one automated repair per guarded episode.

Task bank, selection, and contamination checks. A deterministic task generator produced a fixed manifest of 200 synthetic 'intent_configuration_repair_v1' intents; each manifest entry records initial_state, required_sequence, difficulty annotations (e.g., patterns such as "safe_access_service_transfer" or "rolling_access_vlan_migration"), and a generation_seed for reproducibility. Contamination checks were executed pre‑run (exact SHA256 and n‑gram high‑similarity thresholds); no exact‑match exclusions were flagged and the confirmatory sample remained intact. Representative manifest entries and seeds are archived in the execution task manifest.

Generation semantics and model configuration. Execution adhered to shared_initial_candidate semantics: for each intent exactly one sampled initial generation was produced and deterministically reused for both baseline and guarded episodes. The declared generator was gpt‑5‑mini via the hosted adapter 'openai_responses'; execution/model_configuration.json records declared_model_version = "gpt‑5‑mini" and temperature = null (unset). We explicitly state that temperature = null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling and does not imply temperature = 0; nondeterministic sampling remains possible. The adapter audit shows hosted_model_call_event_count = 200 and a single stage labeled shared_initial_generation = 200, consistent with the preregistered sampling semantics.

Validator and repair pipeline. Scoring used deterministic_netops_validator_v5 with scoring_rule = 'full_intent_constraint_validation' to produce binary executable/invalid labels. Per the preregistration the guarded arm was permitted up to one automated repair attempt; baseline reused the shared sampled candidate without repair. Under shared_initial_candidate semantics the guarded condition can only alter outcomes by applying the repair to that same candidate when the validator flags a violation. All per‑episode validator traces (validation_before, validation_after), normalized_configuration fields, and repair metadata (repair_prompt_sha256, repair_applied flags) were archived in execution/scoring/*.json.

Analysis procedures and reproducibility mapping. The primary analysis used the exact McNemar two‑sided test on the paired contingency table and the paired bootstrap percentile CI (seed and resample counts as above). The primary analysis used the complete_pair_primary rule (exclude incomplete pairs); sensitivity analyses were preregistered for failure‑as‑zero mappings. All analysis artifacts are archived (paired_contingency_table.csv, condition_summary.csv, missingness_summary.csv, contamination_summary.csv) and the deterministic reconciliation report verifies internal accounting and provider audit fields (model_calls_used, cache_miss_count, stage_counts). Key artifact references appear in the archived bundle (execution/raw_results.jsonl; execution/task_manifest.jsonl; execution/model_configuration.json; execution/scoring/; analysis/*).
sections.results:
Execution accounting and deterministic reconciliation. The adapter executed the preregistered plan to completion: planned_episode_count = 400, completed_episode_count = 400, failed_episode_count = 0. Because one shared initial generation per pair was produced and reused for both conditions, model_calls_used = 200. The deterministic reconciliation artifact confirms complete_pairs = 200, baseline_success_count = 200, guarded_success_count = 200, and provider audit values cache_miss_count = 200 and stage_counts.shared_initial_generation = 200; all deterministic consistency checks passed.

Primary inferential outcomes. The observed paired contingency table is n11 = 200, n10 = 0, n01 = 0, n00 = 0 (baseline_success_count = 200/200; guarded_success_count = 200/200). Exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. The paired bootstrap (bootstrap_seed = 1729; resamples = 10,000) paired‑difference 95% percentile CI = [0.0, 0.0]. These numeric outputs and the CSV artifacts are archived under analysis/ and match the confirmatory_results record in analysis/results.json.

Repair activity and representative diagnostics. Across the confirmatory sample repair_attempt_count = 0 and repair_applied_count = 0. The guarded pipeline never applied a repair because all shared initial candidates passed deterministic_netops_validator_v5 checks. Representative per‑episode JSON artifacts (for example, execution/scoring/task‑000004‑baseline.json and task‑000004‑guarded.json) show identical shared_initial_candidate content and identical validation_before.normalized_configuration and validation_after.normalized_configuration fields for both arms. Missingness summary reports zero failed or unscorable episodes; analysis/missingness_summary.csv records complete_pairs = 200 and zeros elsewhere. Deterministic reconciliation confirms consistent episode accounting and no cross‑condition cache reuse. The provider audit shows completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 200 and failed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 0.

sections.discussion:
Causal interpretation under shared_initial_candidate semantics. The shared_initial_candidate execution semantics isolate downstream validator/repair effects on the same sampled candidate by construction. Because every shared candidate passed the deterministic validator, there was no opportunity for the guarded pipeline to alter any outcome; therefore the observed paired difference of 0.0 is an artifact‑grounded null result about this specific estimand (validator/repair effect on each sampled candidate) rather than general evidence that GVR is unnecessary. The provider audit, per‑episode shared_initial_candidate fields, and repair metadata jointly substantiate this causal reading.

Threats to validity and construct limits. Internal validity: the executed sampling semantics intentionally remove generation variability from the estimand, so internal claims are correctly scoped to downstream repair influence only. Construct validity: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 enforces syntactic and workflow constraints encoded from the task payload (required_sequence, allowed_touched_fields, preserve_unspecified_state), but it is an abstraction that does not execute vendor CLI code on real devices; vendor‑specific runtime interactions and some dynamic failure modes (timing, transient state) are therefore not represented. External validity: the run used a single declared model/provider (gpt‑5‑mini via openai_responses), a synthetic task bank, and a single validator implementation; extensions to other models, real device testbeds, or operator workflows require further preregistered runs. Conclusion validity: the degenerate contingency table contains zero discordant pairs, leaving no empirical basis in this run to estimate repair efficacy under independent sampling; a different estimand (e.g., independent per‑condition sampling) is required to create discordant opportunities where repair can act.

Operational implications and precise follow‑on designs. The run validates an end‑to‑end artifacted evaluation pipeline (preregistration, contamination checks, shared_initial_candidate semantics, deterministic validator traces, per‑episode JSON artifacts, deterministic reconciliation). To evaluate repair efficacy under realistic generation variability and stress, we recommend preregistered designs that change the estimand as follows: (1) independent per‑condition first‑pass sampling so baseline and guarded each receive an independent sampled candidate (this permits repair to change outcomes when only the guarded candidate is invalid); (2) targeted high‑difficulty or adversarial subsets of the task bank to increase expected validator flags; (3) explicit numeric sampling‑parameter sweeps (set concrete temperature values instead of leaving temperature = null) recorded in model_configuration.json; (4) multi‑model and multi‑provider sampling to assess generality; (5) elevate validator fidelity by incorporating vendor CLI semantics or packet‑level emulation to test repairs against runtime behavior. Each recommended change is artifact‑specified and requires a new preregistration because it alters the estimand and statistical analysis plan.

Reproducibility and artifact guidance. All primary artifacts required to reproduce the executed estimand are archived: the preregistration identifier (PREREG‑CAND‑001‑VER‑GVR‑2026‑09‑01), execution/raw_results.jsonl (raw per‑episode records), execution/task_manifest.jsonl (deterministic task bank with generation_seeds), execution/model_configuration.json (declared model and temperature = null), execution/scoring/*.json (per‑episode validator traces), and analysis/* CSVs and JSON reconciliation artifacts. These artifacts jointly enable independent reanalysis of the specific shared_initial_candidate estimand executed here without ambiguity about sampling semantics. For reviewers and future experimenters: inspect per‑episode scoring JSONs to verify shared_initial_candidate equivalence between arms and to confirm repair flags and repair_applied indicators.
sections.conclusion: We executed a fully preregistered paired confirmatory experiment designed to measure validator/repair effects when the same single LLM candidate per intent is deterministically reused across baseline and guarded conditions (shared_initial_candidate semantics). With gpt‑5‑mini as declared generator and deterministic_netops_validator_v5 as scorer, every shared initial candidate in the confirmatory sample passed validation and no repairs were attempted; guarded and baseline outcomes were therefore identical on the executed estimand (paired difference = 0.0; McNemar p = 1.0; bootstrap CI = [0.0, 0.0]). This artifact‑grounded null result speaks narrowly to downstream validation/repair influence on the exact sampled candidates produced under the deployed sampling semantics and model settings, not to the broader question of whether GVR pipelines reduce misconfiguration rates under independent sampling, adversarial conditions, or higher‑fidelity validators. We archive full artifacts and recommend follow‑on preregistered experiments that alter sampling semantics and validator fidelity to create the conditions where repairs can empirically change paired outcomes.

limitations: Shared_initial_candidate semantics: a single sampled initial generation was reused across baseline and guarded conditions; this design measures validator/repair effects only and cannot detect differences caused by independent per‑condition sampling or prompt engineering.

Temperature unset (temperature = null) in the archived model configuration: null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling and does not imply temperature = 0; sampling nondeterminism may still have occurred during the single sampled generation.
Single model and single hosted provider: results reflect gpt‑5‑mini under the archived adapter; generalization to other models or model families is unsupported by these artifacts.

Synthetic task bank and validator abstraction: tasks were synthetic 'intent_configuration_repair_v1' items and the deterministic validator is an abstraction; realistic vendor CLI idiosyncrasies, emergent runtime interactions, and hardware effects were not executed on live devices.

No observed validator failures: all initial candidates were validator‑valid, so the experiment could not assess the repair step's effectiveness; the null effect therefore reflects the task bank and sampling semantics rather than evidence that GVR is unnecessary in general.
